messages.subject: Re: Is it possible to output more than the top six elite configurations?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to output more than the top six elite configurations?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Daniel,

By default, the number of elite configurations is dynamic, they are the survivors of the race and they can be as few as one and as many as --min-survival. If you increase --min-survival to 10 you may get 10 or less. On the other hand, all configurations ever generated and their results are saved in the logFile, so you can always select a subset of those sorted by some criteria (by default, irace uses the sum of ranks). See the user guide https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/irace/vignettes/irace-package.pdf sections 9.2 and 9.3. I hope this answers your question.

Cheers,

Manuel.

messages.subject: Re: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
messages.subject_clean: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Manuel,

What I mean is that it is possible to set the seed for irace each time irace is run, rather than accepting the randomly generated seed, so that a run is repeatable.  I provide a seed as a command line argument to irace, for example:
$ IRACE_HOME/bin/irace --seed 130932630

What I am asking is: how many times (each time with a different seed) should I run irace to get a good sample of the parameters that are being tuned?

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.subject: Re: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
messages.subject_clean: Acceptable number of different random seeds to use?
messages.body_plain:
I understand now. That is as difficult to answer as how many runs you need to get a good estimation of the mean performance of any stochastic algorithm: It depends. We usually do 25 or 30 runs as a rule of thumb for comparing different irace variants. But if my goal was to find very good configurations, and I don't care about estimating irace's average performance, then I would probably increase the budget of each run and reduce the number of runs to 5 or 10.  If one has little total budget and a large parameter space, it may be better to do one long run than many short ones. I don't think there is an easy answer available at the moment.

Cheers,

Manuel.

similar ones are answered there.

messages.subject: Benchmarks for irace testing
messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

We are in the search of benchmarks to test new improvements on irace!

I wanted to ask if some of you have algorithms that could be used for testing,
all types of algorithms are welcome and the only requirements are that they should execute
without major problems and their setup should not be very complex.

For now, we would need:
1. Source code (if compilation is required)
2. Set of instances (test and training)
3. Parameter space definition

If you are interested, we can keep you informed about the best parameter settings we find and
their performance.

If you want to collaborate with your algorithm, please contact me:
leslie...@gmail.com

Thanks!

Leslie.

messages.subject: Re: [irace-package] question of ACOTSP examples
messages.body_plain:
Dear Zhenxi,

I think the default time limit of each target-runner run of the ACOTSP example is 60s, multiplied by 5000 runs; it is much more than 15h if not parallelised. What do you mean by the best result? The best configurations look ok to me.

Regarding how to convert the ACOTSP example to your case, please take a look at the user guide. Each element is explained there, otherwise, let us know.

In a nutshell, if you use default options for the rest, you need to define in the scenario file the budget, put your training instances in ./Instances,  and you need to write a parameters.txt and a target-runner. In the most basic case, that's all. If you know python, you can write your target-runner in python.

Cheers,

Manuel.
